title: Reaction Quotient and Equilibrium Constant Ratio Determines Reaction Direction
lead: A mixture that is not at equilibrium has a reaction quotient Q, and the reaction has an equilibrium constant K. Comparing the two tells which way the reaction will run from where it starts.
notes: The book prints no credits for this page.
exercise_notes: The book sets no exercise here; the one exercise and its solution are AI-written, from the standard reaction Gibbs energy the book gives for ammonia in Section 26.6. Numeric answers accept a 2% tolerance.

exercises.source_id: A comparison of $Q$ with $K$ indicates which way the reaction shifts
exercises.prompt:
For N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) at 298.15 K, $K = 5.81\times10^{5}$. A mixture holds NH₃ at 10 bar and N₂ and H₂ at 1 bar each.

  1. What is the reaction quotient $Q$ (pressures in bar)?
  2. What is $\kDeltarG$ for this mixture? Which way does the reaction run?

parts.hint: Products over reactants, each pressure raised to its coefficient.

answer.solution:
(a) $Q = \dfrac{P_{\text{NH}_3}^2}{P_{\text{N}_2}P_{\text{H}_2}^3} = \dfrac{10^2}{(1)(1)^3} = 100$.

(b) $\kDeltarG = \kR\kT\ln(Q/K) = (8.314)(298.15)\ln\left(\dfrac{100}{5.81\times10^{5}}\right) = (2479\ \text{J/mol})(-8.67) = -21.5$ kJ/mol. $Q < K$ and $\kDeltarG < 0$, so the reaction runs forward, making more NH₃.
